rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that after a case outcome (for example a job becoming permanent) the case ends, or else, when a rating or other stated condition holds, it keeps going and returns to an earlier activity to receive further items: Model the outcome as an exclusive gateway after the activity that produces it. Route the ending branch to an end event. Route the continuing branch back to the earlier activity through an exclusive merge gateway placed before that activity. Trace the cycle: every merge gateway on it must have an outgoing path that reaches an end event through the outcome gateway's ending branch, so the cycle can be exited and is not a closed loop.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that after a case outcome (for example a job becoming permanent) the case ends, or else, when a rating or other stated condition holds, it keeps going and returns to an earlier activity to receive further items

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a participant must confirm receipt of something sent to it, or must give a score or assessment of a submitted item or of a counterpart, as a required action of that participant: Model each such stated required action as its own task in the lane of the participant who performs it, placed on the sequence flow where the description places it. Do not omit the action, do not replace it with an intermediate catch event, and do not merge it into another task. Use a task type that matches the described work: a service task only when the description says the step is automated, otherwise a user task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant must confirm receipt of something sent to it, or must give a score or assessment of a submitted item or of a counterpart, as a required action of that participant

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a named actor performs an action that is part of the process, such as submitting a request or signing up: Model that action as a task whose label keeps the actor and the action verb and object as written in the description, for example 'Actor verb object', rather than a shortened verb-object label that drops the actor. Keep the task after the start event that the description implies, and do not replace it with a separate start event or a user task that repeats the actor's action.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant performs a named action on a stage of the process or on another party, and the generated task label uses a related verb that names a different action or a different stage of that same object

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description names an action that a participant performs on a business object, using a specific verb (for example 'enter', 'submit', 'rate' or 'negotiate'): Label the corresponding user task with the verb and object the description uses for that action. Do not replace the verb with a synonym or a broader verb that changes what the action means, and do not add a state or outcome the description does not state.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names an action that a participant performs on a business object, using a specific verb (for example 'enter', 'submit', 'rate' or 'negotiate')

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a flow ends when one condition holds, and that under a second, alternative condition the flow returns to an earlier ongoing activity that keeps delivering new items, so the two outcomes would be reunited before the flow ends: Model the ending outcome as its own branch that leads directly to an end event. Model the returning outcome as a sequence flow back to the earlier ongoing activity. If the two outcomes are reunited by a merge gateway, the merged path must still have a route to an end event: give the returning path its own decision that can lead to an end event, or do not merge it into the ending path at all. Verify that every merge gateway has an outgoing route to an end event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a flow ends when one condition holds, and that under a second, alternative condition the flow returns to an earlier ongoing activity that keeps delivering new items, so the two outcomes would be reunited before the flow ends

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a later step happens only if a stated condition holds, and it gives or implies an alternative outcome for when the condition does not hold: Model the decision as an exclusive gateway placed immediately before the conditional step. Label each outgoing flow with the condition from the description, route the alternative outcome to its own end or continuation, and do not drop the not-taken branch.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a participant must keep reporting an activity it has performed after sending something, and that this reporting obligation ends or no longer applies when a later stated condition holds

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a meeting or interview between two parties can be negotiated or arranged, so the agreed meeting will later be carried out by a participant: Model the negotiating or arranging as its own step, such as a task or an event for the request. Also model the meeting itself as a separate user task named after the meeting that the participant performs, placed after the agreement. Do not let the request or negotiation step stand in for the meeting, and do not fold the meeting into a gateway question.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that a meeting or interview between two parties can be negotiated or arranged, so the agreed meeting will later be carried out by a participant
